children: European wheat fell on Friday in light trade as traders positioned themselves ahead of the release of U.S. government grain forecasts later in the day.
on Paris-based Euronext, was down 1.8% at €240.75 a metric ton at 1500 GMT.
The benchmark contract had fallen to a two-week low earlier in the session at €240.25, down from a contract high of €259.25 last week.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's supply and demand forecasts on Friday has encouraged profit taking by investors who have built up a large long position in wheat.
In addition, diplomatic moves to end Russia's war with Ukraine had weighed on prices.
Commerzbank raised its year-end wheat price forecasts, citing ongoing attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other's ports, it said on Friday.
at the end of the year at $7 per bushel, up from $6.50 projected previously, and Euronext wheat
at €240 per ton, up from €220 previously.

“The market continues to swing between hopes for a safe shipping deal in the Black Sea, which is bearish, and reports of continued Russian and Ukrainian attacks on ports and shipping, which is bullish,” a German trader said.
Egyptian and Libyan importers showed interest in small volumes of 11.5% protein wheat at $300–$305 a ton c&f for September/October shipment.

A trader said Pakistan's 750,000-ton wheat tender next week is expected to draw mainly Romanian and Bulgarian offers, possibly including Ukrainian wheat moved overland into Romania.     However, Pakistan may cancel if prices come in well above $300 a ton c&f.
More difficulties for Germany’s grain logistics were reported as falling river Rhine water levels meant ships could only sail partly-loaded with transport costs rising.
